'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against infrastructure]]
***[[8 July 2024 Ukraine missile strikes]]
****[[Russia]] launches a massive [[missile]] attack striking residential buildings and [[civilian]] [[infrastructure]] in cities across [[Ukraine]], including the [[Okhmatdyt]] children's hospital in [[Kyiv]]. At least 47 people are killed and 189 others are injured as a result of the strikes. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cl4y1pjk2dzo (BBC News)]
**[[Poland–Ukraine relations]]
***[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and [[Polish Prime Minister]] [[Donald Tusk]] sign a security agreement in [[Warsaw]], [[Poland]], allowing Poland to shoot down Russian missiles inside Ukrainian [[airspace]]. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3883098-zelensky-on-security-agreement-poland-will-be-able-to-shoot-down-russian-missiles-in-skies-over-ukraine.html (Ukrinform)]
*[[M23 offensive (2022–present)|M23 offensive]]
**A [[United Nations]] report formally accuses the [[Uganda People's Defence Force|Ugandan military]] of providing support to the [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebel group]] in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. However, [[Uganda]] denies the claims. The report also claims that between 3,000 to 4,000 [[Rwanda]]n soldiers are fighting alongside the M23 rebels. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/uganda-provided-support-m23-rebels-congo-un-report-says-2024-07-08/ (Reuters)] [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20240708-rwandan-soldiers-fighting-with-m23-rebels-in-dr-congo-says-un-report (France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Thousands of [[Samsung Electronics]] workers begin a three-day [[industrial action|strike]] in [[South Korea]] over demands for better pay and more [[annual leave]]. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/samsung-workers-union-south-korea-kicks-off-three-day-strike-2024-07-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Paramount Global]] agrees to merge with [[Skydance Media]] in a $28 billion deal. [https://apnews.com/article/paramount-skydance-redstone-entertainment-merger-8ba177aebe4ec6c3152e5b8ef82a72e0 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Beryl]]
***Three people are killed in [[Houston]], [[Texas]], [[United States]], as Hurricane Beryl makes landfall in Texas as a [[Category 1 hurricane]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/live-blog/rcna160654 (NBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/hurricane-beryl-expected-weaken-quickly-it-churns-across-texas-2024-07-08/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2024 peace missions by Viktor Orbán]], [[China–Hungary relations]]
***[[Prime Minister of Hungary|Hungarian Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] makes an unannounced "peace mission" to [[Beijing]], [[China]], to meet with [[President of China|Chinese President]] [[Xi Jinping]] following an unannounced meeting with [[Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] on Friday. [https://thehill.com/homenews/ap/ap-international/ap-hungarys-orban-makes-surprise-visit-to-china-after-trips-to-russia-and-ukraine/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Brazil–Palestine relations]], [[Palestine–Uruguay relations]]
**[[Brazil]] adopts a [[free trade agreement]] with the [[Palestinian Authority]] and ratifies an agreement with the [[Mercosur]] trade bloc. [[Uruguay]] also backs the deal with Palestine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/brazil-adopts-free-trade-with-palestinian-authority-show-support-2024-07-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[India–Russia relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of India|Indian Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] visits [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], for the first time since the start of the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/8/indias-modi-makes-first-russia-visit-since-ukraine-invasion (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Japan–Philippines relations]]
**[[Japan]] and the [[Philippines]] sign a [[Reciprocal Access Agreement]] which allows the deployment of [[Japan Self-Defense Forces|Japanese forces]] to the Philippines for [[military exercise]]s. It will come into force after both countries' legislatures [[ratify]] it. [https://apnews.com/article/japan-philippines-reciprocal-access-agreement-0e37d57563d475d7507f1647b440e4c2 (AP)]
*[[Poland–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] announces a second $2 billion loan to [[Poland]] to support modernization of its military. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-announces-second-2-billion-military-loan-deal-poland-2024-07-08/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**[[Boeing]] agrees to plead guilty to a criminal [[fraud]] [[conspiracy]] charge to avoid going on trial in the United States on charges related to two fatal crashes involving its [[Boeing 737 MAX|737 MAX]] aircraft in 2018 and 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjjjj85z0lno (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 French legislative election]]
**[[President of France]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] rejects the resignation of [[Prime Minister of France|Prime Minister]] [[Gabriel Attal]], who is requested to stay on temporarily to ensure the stability of the country. [https://apnews.com/article/france-elections-right-left-macron-32fe723ea2a592e7ce243f68a89729a2 (AP)]
